Chapter 232: Who Knew Matchmaking Corners Already Existed Back Then?

People's Park, Heming Tea House.

Chen Guiliang skimmed the foam from his tea with the lid of his bowl. "What kind of business are you thinking of starting?"

"Buying a clothing factory," Qiao Na said.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Where?"

"Hangcheng," Qiao Na replied. "From last year to now, two or three hundred small and medium-sized clothing factories in Hangcheng have gone bankrupt one after another. You can get a ready-made factory building and machinery for a very low price. Plus, the government is giving it the green light all the way!"

Chen Guiliang was actually unaware of this. He asked, "Why are so many going bankrupt?"

Qiao Na explained in detail, "In January last year, the global textile quota system was suspended, and exports from Hangcheng surged in the short term. A lot of business owners jumped at the opportunity to open clothing factories, and everyone flocked to export apparel. But then Europe and the US urgently initiated special safeguard measures, imposing limits on Chinese textiles, and even launched many anti-dumping lawsuits."

With all that happening, it would be a surprise if clothing factories didn't go bankrupt on a massive scale.

Last year, it wasn't just Hangcheng that saw a wave of new clothing factories; coastal apparel manufacturing bases were all building new plants. The sudden trade safeguard measures from Europe and the US led to a huge backlog of textile exports.

And just at that moment, another blow came from within.

CCTV exposed the pollution of the Qiantang River, forcing local governments to implement environmental protection measures. In the Xiao-Shao area alone, 87 printing and dyeing factories were shut down.

The surviving raw material factories had to spend a huge sum on environmental upgrades.

This led to a shortage in fabric supply, causing delays in delivery for clothing factories and increasing the default rate by at least 15%. Moreover, the rising cost of raw materials further squeezed the profit margins of clothing factories.

A triangular debt crisis also erupted, and over 30% of the small factories had their cash flow cut off.

"You want to get into the clothing business at a time like this?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Qiao Na smiled. "Ten thousand trees will spring up before the sickened tree."

"You want to make womenswear?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Hangcheng had been building its reputation as the "Capital of Womenswear" for several years, and the title was gradually becoming well-known.

Qiao Na shook her head. "I wouldn't dare do womenswear. The impact of international brands these past two years has pushed all the local womenswear brands into wholesale markets. 70% of the womenswear in shopping malls are foreign brands."

"Then what will you make?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Qiao Na said, "Children's wear. Right now, the competition is fierce for both menswear and womenswear. Only children's wear still has a sufficient market."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What about your Taobao store?"

"I'll keep that running too," Qiao Na sighed. "With everything that happened last year, the prices of low-to-mid-range clothing, both online and offline, have plummeted. You can get stock for dirt cheap, and more and more people are opening Taobao stores. To snatch customers and clear inventory, some are selling ten shirts for 100 yuan, with free shipping to major cities!"

Chen Guiliang asked, "What's your development plan?"

Qiao Na said, "First, I'll buy a small factory. I've looked into it; the new owner isn't responsible for the triangular debt or back pay. The government will step in and force a resolution. I'll work with stall owners at Sijiqing on one hand, and on the other, I'll continue to sell these clothes on Taobao, trying to clear out the inherited inventory as much as possible. If I can't sell it all, I'll just donate it to children in mountainous regions."

"The initial phase has three steps."

"The first step is to supply unbranded goods to the Sijiqing stalls, while also selling directly through my own Taobao store. This ensures the workers and machines have something to do."

"The second step is to imitate the styles of major international children's wear brands. I won't make too many at first, just small-scale production with under 10 machines. I'll use my Taobao store to build my own brand, slowly accumulating a reputation and repeat customers."

"The third step is to expand production and design my own styles. Once the brand is well-known enough, I'll try opening physical brand stores."

Chen Guiliang didn't know much about the clothing industry and wasn't interested at all. He just asked, "How much money are you short?"

Qiao Na replied, "I've saved over 60,000 yuan these past two years, and I came back this time to find friends to invest. They're all from wealthy families and don't take investing seriously. Five of them pooled together over 70,000 yuan for me. It's more of a loan, as they can't be bothered to go into business together. The factory I've got my eye on isn't big. At the current market rate, I can probably get it for around 500,000 yuan, and that includes a few months of free rent."

Chen Guiliang didn't agree immediately.

Qiao Na said, "This is a special period. Before the mass bankruptcy of clothing factories, the machinery in the factory alone was worth 600,000 yuan!"

Bian Guanyue, who had been silent all this time, suddenly spoke up, "Sister, I can pitch in 180,000 yuan."

Part of the money Bian Guanyue had lent Chen Guiliang had been used to invest in Bailian Technology, and the rest had already been returned to her.

Although this girl was a rich man's daughter, she wasn't usually a big spender—of course, compared to ordinary students, Bian Guanyue was still quite extravagant.

Chen Guiliang asked with a smile, "Including the money you borrowed from your friends, you only have around 130,000 yuan. If I invest, I'll become the major shareholder. Won't you end up working for me?"

"My Taobao store has to be factored in too," Qiao Na said. "And you can only hold a maximum of 25% of the shares. The rest of the money, I'll consider it a loan from you. If you're not willing, I'll find another way."

"Alright then, we'll do it your way," Chen Guiliang said.

He wasn't investing in the clothing factory, but in Qiao Na herself.

A final-year university student about to graduate, she had already saved over 60,000 yuan through her Taobao store and now dared to borrow money from everyone to open a factory. Even if she failed this time, she'd have a chance to make a comeback in the future.

This kind of person had a promising future.

Chen Guiliang was investing in his personal capacity. His current salary and novel royalties were substantial, so taking out two or three hundred thousand yuan was very easy.

"Next time you get into a fight, think about the consequences," Chen Guiliang said, taking a sip from his teacup.

Qiao Na said, "I know my limits. I didn't go for the kill."

You call that knowing your limits?

Qiao Na asked, "Are you wondering why I got into a fight? And why I didn't ask my family for money to start a business?"

"You don't have to say if you don't want to," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Qiao Na said, "I want my dad to know that I'm no worse than a boy. If boys can fight, so can I. I've been able to fight since I was little. If boys can do business, so can I, and without his help!"

Chen Guiliang wasn't aware of her childhood experiences, so he couldn't rashly judge her as naive.

Qiao Na said, "Let's talk about the shares first. You'll take 25%, and Guan Guan will take 10%. The rest of the money, I'll consider it a loan from you both, and I'll pay interest at the bank's lending rate. After I've finished negotiating with the factory, we can sign the contract and the IOU."

"Okay," Chen Guiliang said, unconcerned.

He had some expectations for this factory, mainly because he wanted to see what Qiao Na could achieve.

Was this some kind of alternative management simulation game?

He hadn't felt this sense of anticipation when investing in Tudou or, later on, Zhubajie.com. Because he already knew how things would turn out.

On the contrary, investing in people like Tao Chenggang and Qiao Na, whom Chen Guiliang didn't know in his previous life, felt particularly interesting.

The sound of a text message came from his phone.

Ao Yanchen had sent a message: "I went to the Innovation Center on business today and came across a new startup. I casually asked about it. The founder is Liu Yan, an alumnus from Peking University. He was involved in the financing and IPOs of Sina and AsiaInfo. He also led AsiaInfo's acquisition of DeKang."

Before the first message was finished, another one followed: "This guy was previously the Vice President and a director at Wang Zhidong's current company. He's now starting his own video website, 6.cn. It's positioned to compete with Tudou. The company isn't even registered yet, but he's already secured angel investment. Should I let the people at Tudou know?"

So 6.cn was born too.

And he got angel investment before even registering the company.

Chen Guiliang didn't pass this news on to Wang Wei, because Tudou's real enemy was Youku.

"Young man, want your ears cleaned?" An old man came over and asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "No, thanks."

The three of them chatted idly as they left the tea house and wandered through People's Park, where they unexpectedly came across a "matchmaking corner."

This thing already existed now?

Curious, Chen Guiliang went closer for a look and found that it was surprisingly respectable, not yet the wishing well it would become more than a decade later.

The first profile was for a woman with pretty good qualifications herself. Her only requirements were a stable job, no family burdens, and a height of over 1.72 meters. Having a marital home was a plus, but if not, they could buy one together. No betrothal gift was required.

"Are you looking for a match?" Bian Guanyue joked.

Chen Guiliang replied with a smile, "Yeah, seeing if there's anyone suitable."

Bian Guanyue said, "Then I'll take a look too. Maybe I can find someone better."
